name: Ehsaas
description:
Ehsaas: come walk through Ajji Mane at The Commons with us

📅 10 October | 📍 The Commons, Bangalore

Ehsaas is Urdu for feeling, for realisation. And we'd love for you to come feel it with us.

Why we're doing this

The desi household look was never a style. It was just how our homes looked, growing up. Then it got called dated, then gaudy, and now everyone is chasing it again. We didn't want to explain it to you. We wanted to invite you back inside it.

The Commons shape-shifts around whatever idea it's holding. This time, the foundation was already here: Ajji Mane, Ajji House itself. So we curated it into an experience you can simply walk into, and know what The Commons truly means.

What you'll experience

Ehsaas is a sensorial walkthrough of an ajji's house, room by room. Every room carries its own smell, built into the space itself. A look at the zones:

Sparsh (touch): Start in the tulsi courtyard. Sit with a potter and shape your own matka, guided from start to finish, with clay on your hands.

Awaaz (sound): Sit a while. Listen to nostalgic audios, the jingles, the suprabhatam in the background, the quiet-loud of a house full of people.

Zaika (taste), curated by Subko: Kaccha mango, pickles laid out for tasting, hot chips in crinkly packets, steel plates, a striped cloth hand towel.

Nazar (sight): Step into a living room pulled straight from your grandmother's house.

And at the end, the memory wall, so you can write down everything the space brought back.

**Your ticket includes Pottery Workshop, Sensorial Experience and F&B**

Entry to the full Ehsaas walkthrough, all zones

The Sparsh pottery workshop, guided by a potter, and the piece to take back home

The Zaika food spread, curated by Subko

Bring your friends, bring your family, bring whoever you'd want next to you in an ajji's living room. We'd love to have you all.

Book your ticket and come Ehsaas with us.

name: Pint of View Lecture Over Drinks: Where Have India’s Vultures Gone?
description:
Welcome to Pint of View, Bangalore’s first-ever community where classroom-styled lectures meet drinks in relaxed spaces.

Vultures have huge cultural value, provide crucial ecosystem services, and even have major human health importance across India! That’s quite apart from their amazing attributes, including exceptional eyesight, soaring abilities and disease resistance.

And yet since the 1990s, India has lost a staggering 99.9% of its main vulture species in just ten years, and four species are now on the verge of extinction. It took some serious detective work to understand why!

Learn how an apparently harmless painkiller drug used for cattle caused havoc for all nine vulture species found in India, and how combined efforts of the scientific community, NGOs and especially the Indian Government have been tackling the challenge of saving Asia’s vultures from extinction.

It’s an extraordinary story, which isn’t over yet. Chris has been working to coordinate conservation efforts for these often-misunderstood birds for well over 20 years, and for other endangered species for his entire career. Come and learn about their importance, and perhaps through understanding this better there may be ways you can help turn their fortunes around?

**About the Speaker**

Chris is Globally Threatened Species Officer for the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds and since 2004 has coordinated Asian Vulture work.

He is Advisor to SAVE (Saving Asia’s Vultures from Extinction), a consortium of 32 organisations committed to conserving vultures. Chris is also Co-Chair of the IUCN Vulture Specialist Group (VSG) since 2011.

He has been based in Bangalore, India with his family since 2013. He has also worked on Northern Bald Ibis and other Globally threated species.

Chris was awarded an MBE by Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth in 2022 for services to vulture conservation and the environment.

name: Pint of View Lecture Over Drinks: Where Do Songs Come From?
description:
Welcome to Pint of View, Bangalore’s first-ever community where classroom-styled lectures meet drinks in relaxed spaces.

Ever wondered where a song really begins? Is it a hummed melody, a guitar riff, a feeling or just a random idea that refuses to leave your head?

Vasu Dixit and Jishnu Dasgupta, members of acclaimed folk-rock band Swarathma take you on a journey that traces the origins of their songs. In doing so, they will seek to answer the question, "Where do songs really come from?"

While every songwriter or composer has their own process, Swarathma has their own ways of making the songs that since become part of their three studio albums and numerous singles released over the years since 2009. While some songs begin as a hummed melody while on a bike ride, others begin with a guitar riff played at random. How does a kernel of an idea develop into a melody, a groove, a theme, a verse, a chorus and finally, something that connects with music lovers?

Not only will Vasu and Jishnu take you through the band's and their individual approaches to songwriting, they will even attempt a live mini songwriting workshop with the audience, much like a band jamming together.

Who knows what the audience might inspire and create, even as they learn about Swarathma's songwriting journey?

name: Pint of View Lecture Over Drinks: The Birth of a Nation
description:
Welcome to Pint of View, Bangalore’s first-ever community where classroom-styled lectures meet drinks in relaxed spaces.

**About the Lecture**

When the British decided to leave India in 1947, independence was far from a settled question.

Across nearly two-fifths of the subcontinent, hundreds of princely states were ruled by kings, nawabs and maharajas. Many had no intention of simply joining the new India. Some imagined themselves as independent nations. Others were negotiating with the British, Pakistan and the Congress, trying to work out what the end of empire might mean for their thrones.

In the tense weeks between the British announcement of withdrawal and the birth of independent India, the future of the subcontinent hung in the balance.

What happened behind closed doors? How did Sardar Patel and V. P. Menon persuade hundreds of rulers to give up sovereignty? What role did Gandhi, popular movements and public pressure play? And how close was India to breaking apart into a patchwork of independent kingdoms?

Drawing on newly accessible archival material, this lecture enters the rooms where these decisions were being made: secret communications between princes and London, reports from Hyderabad, orders to destroy sensitive documents, and negotiations that could have changed the map of South Asia forever.

In this lecture, awardwinning journalist and author Josy Joseph takes you on the story of the 21 days in which a new nation had to be assembled, state by state, before the clock ran out.

Because India's independence was not simply about ending British rule. It was also about making sure there was an India left to inherit.

**About the Speaker**

Josy Joseph is a writer-journalist based in New Delhi, and the founder of Confluence Media, a platform-agnostic investigative journalism outfit. He is the author of the award-winning A Feast of Vultures: The Hidden Business of Democracy in India (2016) and the critically acclaimed The Silent Coup: A History of India’s Deep State (2021).

Josy has won several awards for his journalism, including the Prem Bhatia Trust’s ‘India’s Best Political Reporter’ in 2010 “for his scoops and revelations, which include a list of scams that have become familiar names in the political lexicon”, as well as the ‘Journalist of the Year’ Ramnath Goenka award in 2013. Josy has exposed some of India’s biggest scandals—among them, the Mumbai Adarsh Housing scam and the 2010 Commonwealth scam—and his stories have played a significant role in impacting the country’s social & political narrative.

He was the National Security Editor of The Hindu newspaper until August 2018, when he left to start Confluence Media. Previously, he worked with The Times of India as its Editor, Special Projects, with Daily News and Analysis (DNA) as an Associate Editor and with several other mainstream publications. At Confluence Media, Josy is experimenting with creating a commercially viable, scalable, quality journalism outfit.

name: How Did Life Originate on Earth? From Forgotten Experiments to New Insights
description: How chemistry turned into biology—that is, how life originated—remains one of science's biggest open questions. I will start by discussing major hypotheses and some pioneering experimental work on how life might have originated on Earth. I will then revisit the remarkable, yet seemingly discredited and subsequently forgotten, experiments from the 1950s on "jeewanu" -- particles of life -- by Krishna Bahadur and S. Ranganayaki, a scientist couple at the University of Allahabad. Building on this forgotten work, my team has launched an original research program that has yielded many new insights and possibilities. I'll conclude with the implications of this discovery and the next steps toward understanding life and its origins.

Calm Your Wits Quizzing is a Bengaluru-based quizzing collective that curates and hosts engaging, beginner-friendly pub quizzes across India. Founded by quizmaster Sanket Mandal, they have expanded beyond the Bengaluru quizzing circuit to host regular events in Mumbai, Pune, Delhi, and Hyderabad. Launched with the intention of avoiding the intimidating archetype of traditional academic trivia, their style leans towards long-form questions, with lots of clues and audio-visual elements thrown in to help participants arrive at the answer. Quizmaster Sanket also draws heavily from humour on social media, cleverly using tweets, Instagram reels, and memes to make questions on even the most serious of topics. It's a way of reminding people that all that doomscrolling can actually come in handy, and that knowledge can come from anywhere if we're open to the possibilities. Expect questions that keep you guessing, hints that reward lateral thinking, and a few intentional misdirects that may have you arguing with your teammates. Come early, and come curious.

name: Fossil Hunting Expedition - Ariyalur Cretaceous Coast
description:
**Around 70–100 million years ago, South India’s coastline ran through what is now Ariyalur, Tamil Nadu. A warm, shallow sea covered the land, home to ammonites, sea snails, oysters, sea urchins and sharks. When these animals died, they sank into the seabed and were buried in mud and lime. Over millions of years, these layers hardened into rock, while the sea retreated and the seabed became land.**

**Today, monsoon rains expose fossils across Ariyalur’s gullies and ravines, making it one of India’s richest fossil regions. The area has also yielded dinosaur bones and eggs.**

Above Zenith’s first fossil hunting expedition. Over one weekend, you will hunt for fossils at two sites with geologists and paleontologists, learn how to identify and record what you find, and take your finds home.

**What you might find:**

**Ammonites, Belemnites, Gastropods, Bivalves & oysters, Sea urchins, Fossilised wood and Shark teeth.**

**Highlights:**

1. Two fossil hunting sessions, at a younger and an older rock formation
2. A fossil museum visit to see the region's best specimens
3. A limestone mine or cement plant visit (subject to permission)
4. A personal fossil hunting kit to keep
5. A geology session on reading rock layers and identifying your finds
6. A review of the weekend's finds with the resource people
7. Gangaikonda Cholapuram, a 11th century Chola temple and UNESCO World Heritage Site

**Itinerary:**

**Day 0 · Friday, 16 October**

From Bangalore, we drive overnight to Ariyalur.

**Day 1 · Saturday, 17 October**

**Fossil Hunt 1 · 8:45 am to 10:45 am**

**Fossil museum · 11:15 am to 12:45 pm**

**Geology session · 4:30 pm to 6:30 pm**

**Day 2 · Sunday, 18 October**

**Fossil Hunt 2 · 6:15 am to 9:15 am**

**Finds review · 11:00 am to 12:30 pm**

**Limestone mine or cement plant · 2:00 pm to 3:30 pm**

**Gangaikonda Cholapuram · 4:15 pm to 6:00 pm**

**Dinner and departure**

**Day 3 · Monday, 19 October**

Drop-offs between 4:30 am and 5:30 am

This trip is open to all ages: families, kids and adults. No background in science is needed, just curiosity.
